rationale: PINS the FALLBACK ARM of the module-edge source rule — the arm no other protobuf fixture reaches, because every other one declares a package. Since pass 16 the `imports`/`exports` SOURCE is the file's own `package` namespace symbol, which this analyzer already publishes and already hangs the file's top-level declarations from; a file with no package has no such symbol, so the source falls back to the file's basename and `metadata.moduleOwner` reads `basename` rather than `package`. Both arms are needed to tell a correct analyzer from two wrong ones: an analyzer that always used the package would publish an edge whose source is the EMPTY STRING here, and an analyzer that had never made the change would publish `module-edge-source-fallback.proto` here while every other fixture still passed, because the other nine all declare a package. The corpus sizes both arms — 810 of 821 files declare a package, 11 do not, and 5 of the 1,561 `imports` edges come from the 11 (`script/m14/protobuf-module-edge-sources.mts`). This fixture also pins the second consequence of having no package: the file's top-level declaration has NO owner, so it gets NO `contains` edge, and its ids carry no package prefix. PASS 16 ADDENDUM, recorded because it happened: these line numbers were first authored as 13/17/18 and the fixture FAILED, because the header comment was miscounted rather than the file read. That is the authoredBeforeAnalyzerRun discipline working — the expectations were derived by reading the source, reading it wrong produced a red row, and the alternative available to me was to rewrite the fixture until it matched the analyzer, which is the only outcome the discipline exists to prevent.

expectSymbols.name: Orphan
expectSymbols.note: a message declared in a file with no package. Its id carries no prefix, which is what makes this file distinguishable from every other fixture here.

forbidSymbols.note: no symbol with an empty name. The failure mode this fixture exists to catch is a module edge whose source is the empty string, which a package-less file produces if the analyzer reads `pkg` without checking it — and an empty SOURCE is an endpoint the graph cannot walk.

forbidSymbols.name: package
forbidSymbols.note: this file declares no package, so no `namespace` symbol may be published for it. One that was would be a symbol the file does not declare.

expectRelationships.note: THE fallback row. The source is the file's BASENAME because the file declares no package and therefore publishes no namespace symbol to hang the edge on. `metadata.moduleOwner: "basename"` is asserted rather than inferred: it is the field that distinguishes this edge from the 1,556 whose source is a package, so a consumer can tell an external-by-necessity source from a resolved one without re-deriving it from the file.

the field's declared type is a message, so it is a reference and not a scalar. This row is here so the fixture also pins that a package-less file resolves cross-file type references NORMALLY — losing the package costs the module edge its owner, not its type resolution.

forbidRelationships.note: the empty source. `pkg` is "" for this file and an analyzer that used it without a length check would publish this edge from nothing. An edge whose source is the empty string is a node the index does not hold.
this file has no `import public`, so there is nothing to re-export. An `exports` row here would mean a modifier was inferred from something other than the declaration.

supersession 2026-10-27: this row's label moved from uses to references per the 1:1 relabel rule (PB-REL-5's uses role retired; the fleet's type-position contract: a field's declared type NAMES a type the way a query would). The forbid pins the RETIRED label so a silent widening back to uses goes red.
